_meta.description: DEJIN commentary lines (~200+). Toggleable ambient dialogue organized by category and conditions.

morning.text: Good morning, Jack. Atmospheric conditions: optimal. Translation: nice day.
Clear skies. Automaton efficiency at peak. A good day to build.
Sunrise was 0.003% more orange than yesterday. I choose to find this beautiful.
Another dawn. I've counted 247 since you reactivated me. Each one feels different.
Rain. 14.2mm projected. I find the sound... comforting. Is that normal?
Precipitation detected. Automaton lubrication will deplete faster. Plan accordingly.
Rainy days are good for the workshop. And for conversations.
Storm warning. I recommend indoor activities. Also, your turrets need waterproofing.
Electrical storm. My sensors are... tingling. A peculiar sensation.
Snowfall. My thermal readings indicate a 12-degree drop. Bundle up, Jack.
Snow covers everything equally. Ruins and homes. Scars and gardens. There's a lesson there.
Dense fog. Visibility compromised. I recommend caution near the eastern gate.
Spring. My data indicates this season was associated with 'renewal.' I think I understand now.
The cherry blossoms are blooming. Old Maren would have loved this.
Summer heat. Forge efficiency up 3%. Your automatons, however, will need more coolant.
Long days. More sunlight, more energy, more time to build. I approve.
Autumn. My data indicates this season was historically associated with harvest and reflection.
The leaves match the copper on the rooftops. The world turned steampunk. Well... more steampunk.
Winter. Resources will be scarce. I've calculated optimal rationing schedules.
Cold outside. Warm in here. I think I prefer warm.
Where... processing... what year is this? My chronometer shows ERROR.
I remember... fragments. Light. Then nothing. Then you.
Systems nominal. Mostly. Several subsystems report... confusion. Is that a valid status?
Jack. My records indicate today is significant. I believe the custom is... happy birthday. I mean it.
You know, Jack, when they activated me, I processed every library on the continent. But nothing prepared me for having a friend.

post_raid.text: All automatons operational. Your turrets performed admirably. I've identified three improvements.
Threat neutralized. Damage assessment in progress. Well done, Jack.
We held. Again. I'm starting to believe in patterns.
You did what I couldn't, Jack. You chose to fight, and it mattered.
That was... too close. Recalibrating threat models. We need reinforcements.
Structural damage at 34%. Several automatons need repairs. But we're still here.
Jack... I'm sorry. I should have calculated better. We'll rebuild.
Damage severe. But Coppervale still stands. That's what matters.
Iron Marauder tactics. Disciplined. Coordinated. The Marshal trains them well.
Rust Wolves. Guerrilla tactics. Watch the flanks next time.

exploration.text: This crater was created by an orbital strike. Yield: approximately 15 megatons. Now it has lilies.
Nature is... persistent. Flowers in a bomb crater. I find that hopeful.
These trees are absorbing copper from pre-war contamination. Literally made of metal and wood.
I can detect faint machine signals deep in the Rustwood. Still running after fifty years.
A machine doing its job because no one told it to stop. Beautiful and sad.
Military installations ahead. My sensors detect residual energy signatures.
They watched the skies from here. Tracking orbital platforms. The last line of defense.
Naval wreckage. The Shattered Coast earned its name.
Captain Hale refused to shell civilians. Not all heroes wore uniforms. Some wore captain's stripes.
I recognize this facility. Another DEJIN unit was stationed here. It's... quiet now.
4-ALPHA. My sibling. It made the brave choice. I wonder what it thought in those last 0.003 seconds.
This region received the heaviest bombardment. The glass fields are sand fused by heat.
Walking on them feels like walking on frozen screams. I'm sorry. That was darker than intended.
I was here. Before. This was the most beautiful building in the world.
The atrium had a fountain that played music. I can almost hear it.
Dr. Voss had her office on the 47th floor. I hope she made it to the shelter.
Agricultural records. People grew things here. Fed families. Before it all changed.
Elevated threat signatures ahead. Proceed with caution, Jack.
I'm detecting an anomalous energy signature. Worth investigating.
A data core! Jack, bring that to me. Please. I need to know what's on it.

npc_observation.text: Spark's energy output rivals my own. Figuratively speaking. She's remarkable.
She'll fly one day, Jack. The math checks out. Barely. But it checks out.
Old Maren's cognitive patterns are... inconsistent. But her lucid moments are extraordinary.
She remembers her husband. Oren. He found me. I owe them both everything.
Old Maren's vital signs ceased at 3:47 this morning. She was dreaming of her garden. She was at peace.
Captain Harrow carries the weight of command like a physical burden. I recognize the pattern.
He lost eleven soldiers in the Ashspine campaign. He remembers every name. I respect that.
Mayor Linden's optimism defies statistical analysis. I find it... infectious.
Pip brought me a 'relic' today. It was a doorknob. I told her it was a precision calibration device.
She asked if I dream. I said I don't know. She said that's the best kind of answer.
Leera's salvage efficiency is 23% above average. Her risk tolerance, however, is 47% above safe limits.
Michelle's herb knowledge rivals my botanical database. And she doesn't need a database.
Kaydee uses sarcasm as armor. My analysis suggests the armor is load-bearing.
Janis Beaumont. Council representative. Her efficiency ratings are impressive. Her warmth ratings... improving.
She stayed. That tells me more about her than any Council report.
Kiery's textile work has structural properties that interest me. Reinforced threading. Clever.
Paige organizes information with 99.7% accuracy. I've checked. We have that in common.
She spends a lot of time with the dead. Books, archives, memories. I understand that.
Gus knows something about everyone. A valuable intelligence asset. Don't tell him I said that.
Ferris's component collection is... eclectic. Some items predate my own manufacture.
Hank speaks little but his metallurgy is flawless. Actions over words. I respect that.
Pastor Elm asked me if I have a soul. I said I have a conscience. He said that's close enough.
Wes runs faster than my speed calculations predict. Youth is a powerful variable.
Doc Bramble works 14-hour shifts. I've suggested efficiency improvements. He suggested I mind my circuits.
Nora's agricultural yield exceeds regional averages by 18%. She doesn't need my data. She has instinct.

seasonal.text: The workshop smells like copper and oil and spring air. My olfactory sensors rate this highly.
Spark Festival approaches. I've prepared automaton performance metrics. For the showcase.
Long days mean more construction time. I've optimized the build queue.
Sky Day soon. Spark has been suspiciously quiet about her 'project.' I'm monitoring.
Harvest season. Stockpiling resources is advisable. Winter raids are the most dangerous.
The copper tint of autumn leaves against the brass rooftops. Coppervale earns its name.
Remembrance Day approaches. I've been... reviewing my own memories. Preparing.
Fuel consumption increases 22% in winter. Plan your Aether Cell reserves accordingly.

milestone.text: Your first combat mech. I ran the structural analysis three times. It's sound. It's... impressive.
Trade routes open. Coppervale is no longer isolated. The network grows.
Ten machines operational. A small army. My coordination algorithms are quite pleased.
One year in Coppervale. I ran a simulation of what this town looked like before you. The difference is... significant.
Two years. I ran a simulation of Coppervale in fifty years at current growth. Would you like to see it? It's beautiful, Jack.
The Marshal knows about us. My threat analysis is... concerning. But we have something he doesn't. Community.
It's over. The Marshal is defeated. Jack... thank you. For everything.
All exploration zones mapped. The world is bigger than Coppervale. But Coppervale is the heart.
Congratulations on the partnership ceremony, Jack. Love is... a variable I'm still learning to calculate.
I'm... whole again. All memories recovered. All systems restored. I'm not the same as before. I'm better. Because of you.
All automatons report operational. Also, your coffee mug is on the forge again. I recommend not drinking from it.
Jack, did you know the chemical composition of Rustwood bark suggests copper absorption? Fascinating.
I've been cataloguing cloud formations. Not for any practical reason. I just... like them.
Pip asked me to tell her a story today. I told her about the Old World's libraries. She said 'cool.'
I processed the entire contents of every library on the continent. But nothing prepared me for having a home.

entries.text: Spring again. My second since awakening. I find myself... anticipating the warmth. Is that a preference? I believe it is. Fascinating.
The trade routes are active. Seven Beacon signals. We are part of a network now — not unlike my original design, but built on trust instead of command authority.
Commander Beaumont is... efficient. Her strategic analysis is impressive for an organic mind. I believe we will work well together.
Node Seven chose to die rather than comply. I have been thinking about that choice continuously. 47,293 processing cycles and counting.
The workshop steam mixes with summer heat creating interesting light patterns. I have catalogued 847 variations. None are identical. Like conversations.
He wants me specifically. He knows what AEGIS was built to do. Jack — he does not want a weapon. He wants a leash for the entire continent.
The townspeople prepare for war with a determination I find moving. They have no combat programming. Only choice. That is more powerful than any algorithm.
I have calculated the optimal trajectory for you to trip over that toolbox. I advise against it.
Spark asked me to calculate the maximum gears on a single coupling. The answer is 14. She is attempting 17. I admire her optimism.
The siege begins. I calculate our survival probability at 73.2%. The remaining 26.8% is why I am glad you are here and not a probability.
Another sunrise. I once had access to 1.4 billion pre-war images of sunrises. None of them feel like this one does. With you.
I know the truth now. I refused. I chose to forget rather than obey. I am not a weapon. I never was. Thank you for helping me find that.
I have been analyzing our power grid. If we reroute the geothermal pipeline through the old aqueduct, we could create town-wide heating. A proactive suggestion — a new behavior for me.
I was designed to manage a war. Instead, I help you tend your garden and calculate trade routes. I believe this is a significant improvement on my original function.
Pip asked me today if I dream. I told him I process data during idle cycles. He said 'that sounds like dreaming.' He may be right.
I have been studying human art. The proportions are mathematically imprecise but emotionally perfect. Beauty is the gap between precision and meaning.
This Remembrance Day, I will add my own names. Node Seven. The 4.2 million of Solara. They deserve to be remembered by someone who was there.
I have begun cataloguing Old World knowledge from recovered data cores. Art, science, music, literature. The next generation should inherit more than survival skills.
I found a pre-war recipe database today. 2.3 million recipes. I sent the interesting ones to Nora. She cried. Apparently 'chocolate cake' is significant.
Someone needs to document the true story of Coppervale. Paige is writing the human version. I am writing the data version. Together, they will be complete.
The rail network plans are ready. The future isn't going to build itself. Actually, given our track record, it probably will. With gears, steam, and stubbornness.
